newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore growth may reach seven pct in 1997 - SICC.
newsitem.headline: Singapore growth may reach seven pct in 1997 - SICC.

text.p: Singapore's gross domestic product growth may reach seven percent in 1997 compared with 6.5 percent in 1996, the Singapore International Chamber of Commerce (SICC) said on Wednesday.
"I feel that growth...could well reach seven percent this year, and will certainly achieve six percent," Executive Director Graham Hayward told a luncheon.

He said the main downside risk could be a marked decline in Wall Street, which could trigger a collapse in local stock markets. This would lead to negative business sentiment in the region and elsewhere.
"However, at this point in time, this does not seem very likely and I am therefore relatively bullish on prospects for the economy this year, particularly in the second half," he said.
The Singapore government recently forecast 1997 economic growth at between five to seven percent.
